decisions.finding: The longest option is the right one in all four quiz questions; the learner was choosing by length
decisions.reason: Measured in the file: keyed answer longest in 8 of 10 (all four quiz questions). Ruling R5.
decisions.change: See R5. Every distractor now carries a specific wrong reading with its own reason and numbers.

decisions.finding: Keyed option is the single longest in 8 of the 10 questions
decisions.reason: Same measurement; option length must carry no signal.

decisions.finding: Seg 3 speaks five counts in four sentences while all four boxes are on screen at once
decisions.reason: The ear problem is real. A per-box reveal is not available: the matrix visual has no cue support (validate.py CUE_ITEMS, visuals.js R.matrix), and swapping it for a table would lose the 2x2 picture the assistant prints.
decisions.change: Seg 3 now speaks three counts (141 flagged, 104 caught, 423 missed), in the order of the on-screen columns and with the cells' own words (caught, false alarms, misses, left alone); 37 and 3,436 are left to the screen.

decisions.finding: The narration is a churn course; rotate the spoken example to invalid traffic or video adoption
decisions.reason: Generality is handled by ruling R1. Re-basing the worked example is out of scope: facts.json holds four-box counts and a threshold table only for the churn model (logreg.test, thresholds), and R1 keeps worked numbers on the course tables.
decisions.change: Seg 2 gains the general sentence naming invalid traffic; the recap speaks of 'a report or a vendor'.

decisions.finding: 'On another draw of test advertisers' is unexplained; the idea arrives only in 2-6
decisions.reason: The term is not taught yet (SPEC rule 7). Figures unchanged: uncertainty.precision_at_half_95 = 0.665 to 0.809.
decisions.change: Seg 5: 'with a different set of test advertisers, precision could land anywhere from about 67 to 81 percent. A later lesson shows how we know.' The same phrase is fixed in 2-3 seg 4.

decisions.finding: 'Say no' to rebalancing contradicts the other-ways card that allows resampling the training rows
decisions.reason: The flat refusal was stricter than the truth: reweighting or resampling training rows is legitimate when positives are very few, provided the scores are corrected; the test rows must never be touched.
decisions.change: Seg 7 rewritten: default answer no; on the test rows never; on the training rows a last resort for very rare outcomes, with scores corrected and checked against what happened. The brief says the same.

decisions.finding: Cue markers start at 2 in segs 2 and 6, so the first item may never be revealed while the voice talks about it
decisions.reason: Confirmed in site/public/js/player.js and visuals.js: when a segment has any cue, every item starts hidden, a cue N reveals items 1 to N, and items above the highest cue stay hidden until the segment ends. In seg 2 both cards were blank until the second half; in seg 6 the model's row never appeared while the voice compared it with the rule.
decisions.change: Seg 2: [[1]] added before 'Call every advertiser a stayer'. Seg 6: [[1]] at the start, [[3]] before 'And notice the rule's accuracy', and the table rows reordered (model, hand rule, everyone stays) so each appears when the voice reaches it. Seg 6 spoken text is unchanged, so its audio stands.

rulings.R1: Seg 2: 'That holds for any yes-or-no model: when almost every click is valid, last lesson's invalid-traffic filter could flag nothing and score almost perfectly.' Invalid traffic is named again on purpose: it answers the question the new 2-1 opening leaves open. 2-3 uses video adoption.
rulings.R3: Brief is a slot template, 113 words: [model], [the test period], [cut-off], [outcome], [the common outcome], [rule]. Adds 'print the test row count and the [outcome] rate' so the audit checks can be run.
rulings.R4: Seg 9 is 49 words: what to do when accuracy leads a report, then the pointer to 2-3. Visual kept.
rulings.R5: Keyed longest in 3 of 10 (was 8). Rewritten: all four quiz questions and review 1 variants 1-3 and review 2 variant 3. Two 'nothing is wrong' options replaced (2-2-q2, review 2 variant 3). Review 2 variants 1 and 2 untouched. All keyed positions unchanged.
rulings.R6: Not triggered: the most usable move (four counts with precision and recall beside both baselines) is already the spoken brief, and the training-rows alternative now has its spoken sentence in seg 7. Seg 8 left byte-identical.
rulings.R7: All four audit items were already checkable from the output (counts add up to the row count; caught plus missed equals the churner total; cut-off stated beside both baselines; test churn rate unchanged). Left as they were.
rulings.specific: None listed. Clarity protected as instructed: segs 1, 4 and 8 are byte-identical, and the 95 percent example is kept word for word.

open_questions: Player versus SPEC: SPEC says items without a marker are visible from the start; the player hides every item until the first cue and keeps items above the highest cue hidden to the end. The finding names the same pattern in 2-5 seg 3, 2-6 seg 4 and 3-1 seg 5. Fix the player (applyCues) or the lessons.
The matrix visual cannot build box by box. If you want the reveal the learner asked for, the player needs cue support on matrix cells.
